title: DD engine: cycle detection + lazy population + eviction
description:
## Parent

sutra/v1/5 — PRD: sutra v1 review intelligence engine

## What to build

Add `src/dd/` module implementing the differential dataflow engine. This is the first DD view and proves the full integration pattern. Ingest facts from SQLite (files, symbols, imports, refs), maintain a cycle detection view, expose a query interface. DD graph is lazy-populated on first DD-backed tool call (not on daemon startup or sutra_status). Evict DD state after configurable idle timeout (default 30 min). No DD types leak outside the module — consumers get plain Rust structs.

Reference implementation: `src/bin/dd-spike.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DdEngine` struct with `ingest(facts)`, `update(delta)`, `query_cycles()` interface
- [ ] Cycle detection returns expected cycles for a known fixture codebase
- [ ] Lazy population: DD graph not built until first DD-backed query
- [ ] Eviction: DD graph released after idle timeout, re-query triggers rebuild with same results
- [ ] No DD/timely types in the public interface
- [ ] Tests: cycle detection against fixture, delta update correctness, eviction round-trip

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately. DD is in-memory only, no new tables needed.

Completed:

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — request changes:

[high] Evicted DD engine cannot rebuild on re-query (src/dd/engine.rs:80-85). query_cycles() returns an error when Cold, and evict_if_idle() drops the worker by setting state back to Cold. Because ingest() consumes DdFacts and the engine retains no fact snapshot, a query after eviction cannot rebuild the graph — callers must manually re-ingest. Population is also not lazy: ingest() spawns the worker immediately.

Recommendation: Store latest facts in an evicted/cold-loaded state, make ingest() record facts without spawning the worker, and have query_cycles() warm/rebuild on demand. Add a test that evicts then queries without re-ingesting.
